{{nihongo|'''Hida Shrine'''|斐太神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Miyauchi, {{ill|Myōkō, Niigata|Q279642|qid=Q279642}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|Q132705|qid=Q132705}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine ranking system}} its rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. {{nihongo|'''Hida Shrine'''|斐太神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

It stands facing east on a hill west of the Miyauchi settlement, on the eastern foot of a branch ridge extending from Aota Minamihayama. Around the shrine are the {{ill|Hida Sites|ja|斐太遺跡群|qid=Q85766470|lt=Hida ruins}}; to the north are the {{ill|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun Group|ja|観音平・天神堂古墳群|zh|觀音平和天神堂古墳群|qid=Q17990293|lt=Kannondaira kofun group}}, and to the south the {{ill|Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun Group|ja|観音平・天神堂古墳群|zh|觀音平和天神堂古墳群|qid=Q17990293|lt=Tenjindō kofun group}} (designated a national {{ill|Historic site|Q1081138|qid=Q1081138}} together as "Kannondaira-Tenjindō Kofun Group").

== Enshrined deities ==
With {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}} (Yachihoko-no-Kami) as principal deity, it also enshrines {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|fa|کوتوشیرونوشی|fr|Kotoshironushi|it|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主|ko|고토시로누시|ru|Котосиронуси|simple|Kotoshironushi|th|โคโตชิโรนูชิ|zh|事代主神|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} (Tsumihane Yae Kotoshironushi-no-Kami) and {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto}} (Suwa Ōkami) as {{ill|Aidono|ja|相殿|qid=Q135009883}} deities. These two were moved from other shrines: Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto, also called Yashiro Ōkami/Yashiro Myōjin, is said to have stood until {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 2 ({{ill|1574|ab|1574|af|1574|als|1574|am|1574 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1574|ar|1574|ary|1574|arz|1574|ast|1574|avk|1574|az|1574|azb|۱۵۷۴ (میلادی)|bar|1574|bcl|1574|be|1574|be_x_old|1574|bg|1574|bn|১৫৭৪|bpy|মারি ১৫৭৪|br|1574|bs|1574.|ca|1574|cdo|1574 nièng|ceb|1574|ckb|١٥٧٤|crh|1574|cs|1574|cv|1574|cy|1574|da|1574|de|1574|diq|1574|el|1574|eml|1574|eo|1574|es|1574|et|1574|eu|1574|fa|۱۵۷۴ (میلادی)|fi|1574|fo|1574|fr|1574|frr|1574|fur|1574|fy|1574|ga|1574|gan|1574年|gcr|1574|gd|1574|gl|1574|gv|1574|he|1574|hi|१५७४|hr|1574.|ht|1574 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1574|hy|1574|hyw|1574 թուական|ia|1574|id|1574|ilo|1574|io|1574|is|1574|it|1574|ja|1574年|jv|1574|ka|1574|kaa|1574|kk|1574 жыл|ko|1574년|krc|1574 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1574|la|1574|lb|1574|lij|1574|lmo|1574|lt|1574 m.|lv|1574. gads|mai|१५७४|map_bms|1574|mdf|1574|mg|1574|mhr|1574|mi|1574|min|1574|mk|1574|mr|इ.स. १५७४|mrj|1574 и|ms|1574|my|၁၅၇၄|mzn|۱۵۷۴|nah|1574|nap|1574|nds|1574|new|सन् १५७४|nl|1574|nn|1574|no|1574|nrm|1574|nso|1574|oc|1574|or|୧୫୭୪|os|1574-æм аз|pam|1574|pl|1574|pnb|1574|pt|1574|qu|1574|ro|1574|ru|1574 год|rue|1574|sa|१५७४|sah|1574|scn|1574|sd|1574ع|se|1574|sh|1574.|shn|1574|simple|1574|sk|1574|sl|1574|smn|1574|sq|1574|sr|1574|su|1574|sv|1574|sw|1574|ta|1574|tg|Соли 1574|th|พ.ศ. 2117|tk|1574|tl|1574|tly|1574|tr|1574|tt|1574 ел|uk|1574|ur|1574ء|uz|1574|vec|1574|vi|1574|vls|1574|wa|1574|war|1574|wuu|1574年|xmf|1574|yi|1574|zh|1574年|zh_min_nan|1574 nî|zh_yue|1574年|qid=Q6680}}) at Okazawayama upstream of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yashiro River}}; because this deity is enshrined here, the shrine is popularly called "Yashiro-san." Takeminakata-no-Mikoto is said to have stood on the summit of Aota Minamihayama.

In the past {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Kōtaijin}} was also enshrined. An alternative theory in ''Echigo Kubiki District Gazette Draft'' (1901) introduces another deity theory, Arahito-no-Mikoto. In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|de|Shinsen Shōjiroku|fr|Shinsen shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|ko|신찬성씨록|ru|Синсэн сёдзироку|zh|新撰姓氏錄|qid=Q1045362}}''<ref>''Shinsen Shōjiroku'', section Right Capital, Imperial descent, upper.</ref>, Arahito is described as the fifth-generation descendant of Kose Okarano Sukune, son of {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}}, and ancestor of Kose Hita no Ason and Kose Hita no Omi. Maruyama Motosumi's ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hokuetsu Fudoki Setsuge}}'' (1686) also lists this as the deity. There is also a theory making Kose Okarano Sukune-no-Mikoto the deity (''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|ja|神名帳考証|qid=Q11588824}}'', ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Echigo Yashi}}''), and because Hata no Yashiro no Sukune was Okarano Sukune's elder brother, some argue the co-enshrined Yashiro Myōjin may be Hata no Yashiro no Sukune-no-Mikoto<ref>{{ill|Kurita Hiroshi|ja|栗田寛|qid=Q6536170}}, ''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shingi Shiryo}}'' (compiled 1873).</ref>.

== History ==
[[File:Hida Site, Yashiroyama-B, gaikan.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Hida ruins (national historic site)}}]]
As noted above, present Hida Shrine is a merger of Hida deity (Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto), Yashiro Myōjin, and Suwa Daimyōjin. Of these, the original Hida Shrine (shikinaisha) is said first to have stood on the mountain. On the right bank of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Uchikawa (Niigata)}}, a tributary of Yashiro River, at Tobita Aza Yashikizoe in Myōkō, there was said to be a satomiya with a haiden. The old site is thought possibly to be Miyazawa north of the Samegao Castle ruins west of the shrine<ref name="report">''Shikinaisha Survey Report''.</ref>, but the time and reason for relocation to the current site are unknown. One theory says it was originally called "Hita Myōjin" and changed to "Hida Myōjin" in the {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325|lt=Engi era}} (early 10th century)<ref>''Place Names of Niigata Prefecture''.</ref>.

To the west and north of the present site lie pit-dwelling groups of Uenotaira and Hyakuryōyama (part of the Hida ruins) interpreted as building remains; further north lies Kannondaira Kofun Group, and to the south Yashiroyama pit-dwelling group (also in Hida ruins) and Tenjindō Kofun Group. It has been suggested that the power that built Kannondaira and Tenjindō kofun may have worshipped Hida Shrine<ref name="report"/>. Shrine tradition, however, says Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto came to this region with his child deities Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto and Takeminakata-no-Mikoto, stayed here, taught rice cultivation, and managed the land; at that time he named the area "Hidakami no Kuni" in {{ill|Koshi Province (Japan)|de|Provinz Koshi (Japan)|es|Provincia de Koshi (Japón)|ff|Koshi Province (Japan)|fr|Province de Koshi (Japon)|ja|越国|ko|고시국|nl|Koshi (provincie)|pt|Província de Koshi|simple|Koshi Province (Japan)|zh|越國 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Kosi-kok|zh_yue|越國 (日本)|qid=Q1351611}}, from which the place name "Hida" arose<ref>Historically, "Hida" referred collectively to present Miyauchi, Yukimori, Tobita (in Myōkō) and Inari (in Jōetsu), and there is also a place name "Takami" in Tobita (''Shikinaisha Survey Report'').</ref>. In this account, Ōkuninushi and Takeminakata developed mountains and fields, while Kotoshironushi (Yashiro Myōjin) controlled marshes and rivers and opened waterways.

According to ''{{ill|Daidō Ruijuhō|ja|大同類聚方|qid=Q11433347}}'' of {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} 3 ({{ill|AD 808|Q30366|qid=Q30366}}), this shrine had a special medicine for stroke called "Samizu-yaku," whose formula had been transmitted by {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōanamuji-no-Kami}}; it was also a hereditary medicine of the Ōgami clan, junior district officials of Kubiki District. Later, under the Engi system, Hida deity was listed as a small shrine in Kubiki District, {{ill|Echigo Province|Q666514|qid=Q666514}}; Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto stood as protector of riverbanks deep in Okazawayama upstream of Yashiro River (leaving the river name), and Takeminakata-no-Mikoto stood on Aota Minamihayama summit. Though the date is unknown, they are said to have been merged into Hida Shrine, and traces remain on the summit.

In the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023}}, the shrine was revered by the {{ill|Uesugi clan|Q1150058|qid=Q1150058}}. When Samegao Castle was built on the mountain west of the shrine, Hida Shrine was designated the {{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}} for 128 nearby villages, and shrine lands were donated from villages including Miyauchi, Jingūji, Otsuyoshi, Kagochō, Yukimori, Aota, Inari, Tōkaichi, and Tobita<ref>Except Inari, which belongs to Jōetsu City, all are in Myōkō City.</ref>. In Tenshō 2, {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|Q311080|qid=Q311080}} is said to have merged Yashiro Myōjin (a stone shrine remains at the former site), revering the three deities as protectors of the castle's {{ill|Kimon|Q11673539|qid=Q11673539}} direction. The shrine burned in warfare at Samegao Castle's fall in Tenshō 7 ({{ill|1579|Q6709|qid=Q6709}}), and burned again in {{ill|Meireki|Q1192766|qid=Q1192766}} 2 ({{ill|1656|Q6982|qid=Q6982}}); documents burned with the buildings, so detailed history is unclear.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, in {{ill|Tenna|Q1145289|qid=Q1145289|lt=Tenna}} 3 ({{ill|1683|Q7651|qid=Q7651}}) land survey, the shrine received 5 koku 3 gō of tax-exempt land. After the {{ill|Sakakibara clan|Q2975351|qid=Q2975351}} entered as lords of {{ill|Takada Domain|Q839422|qid=Q839422}} in Echigo, it received continued patronage. The adjacent Jingūji district south of Miyauchi is named for {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Jingūji (Jōetsu)}} temple (now in Teramachi, Jōetsu), formerly this shrine's {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}}, said to have moved to Jōetsu in Edo times<ref name="report"/>.

In December {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}) it was ranked village shrine; on Nov 3, Shōwa 17 ({{ill|1942|Q18625|qid=Q18625}}), promoted to gōsha. Promotion to prefectural shrine was planned for Nov 3, Shōwa 20 but cancelled by defeat in war. On May 11, Shōwa 33 ({{ill|1958|Q5253|qid=Q5253}}), fire completely destroyed the shrine buildings.

== Precincts ==
The honden is 3-by-3 bay, gable-entry {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}}, called "grand-shrine-style Shinmei-zukuri" by the shrine. The haiden is 3-by-4 bay kirizuma-zukuri gable-entry. Both are tile-roofed and connected by a kirizuma-zukuri stone room passage.

A {{ill|Magatama|Q334232|qid=Q334232}} and {{ill|sekitai|Q11586501|qid=Q11586501}} said to have been excavated in the precinct are treasured but undesignated.

== Subsidiary shrines ==
[[File:Hida-jinja (Myoko), Karita-jinja.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Karita Shrine}}]]
Karita Shrine ({{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}), plus stone-hokora Inari and Hachiman shrines are enshrined.

== Festivals ==
At the March 3 fire-quelling festival, "Harukoma dance" is performed at the {{ill|Naorai|Q11581721|qid=Q11581721}} feast: a woman wearing a {{ill|tanzen|Q9210345|qid=Q9210345}} and holding a phallic symbol, and a man in women's {{ill|Zhongyi|Q55358825|qid=Q55358825}} holding a female symbol, red cloth, and bells, dance with faces covered.

== Priests ==
The Kurashina family serves hereditarily. The family claims Fujiwara lineage and says that when {{ill|Emperor Juntoku|Q357249|qid=Q357249}} was exiled to {{ill|Sado Province|Q1063844|qid=Q1063844}}, they moved from Kyoto to Kurashina village in {{ill|Shinano Province|Q289250|qid=Q289250}}, {{ill|Sarashina District, Nagano|Q7423207|qid=Q7423207}} (present Kurashina, {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|Q179757|qid=Q179757}}, Nagano) as communication liaison, settled there, later moved to Echigo, and became priests of this shrine<ref name="report"/>.

== Access ==
* About 35 minutes west on foot from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Myōkō Haneuma Line}} {{ill|Kita-Arai Station|Q5355811|qid=Q5355811}}
* {{ill|Kubikino Bus|Q11265488|qid=Q11265488}} route 48 Hida line<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.joetsu.niigata.jp/soshiki/kotsu/bus-jikoku.html|title=Comprehensive timetable of public transport in Jōetsu City|publisher=Jōetsu City|accessdate=2020-04-02}}</ref> to "Hida Kita Elementary School-mae," then about 8 minutes southwest on foot (weekdays only, few services)
